title: Corporate Tax System Complexity and Investment Sensitivity to Tax Policy Changes

scopes.description: Full author-documented Stata workflow: ordered preparation produces the primary firm-year sample, then runs the primary analysis and supplied stacked DiD branch.

requirements.description: Required 504-file main Orbis firm extract, selected by the author’s documented active-status, geography, company-type, financial-history and ultimate-owner criteria. The code keys by bvdidnumber, filters status and NACE, reshapes wide financial fields into 2012–2019 firm-year rows, drops 2020 onward and retains firms with seven observations. Required variable families include employees, fixed and intangible/tangible assets, cash, total assets, current/noncurrent liabilities, sales, operating profit, pretax profit, tax, net income, employee costs, loans, cost of goods sold and long-term debt; depreciation is supplied through the separate pull. The packaged CSV contains BvD identifiers only.

issues.description: The country-level program reads country_years.dta as the master for a 1:1 countryisocode/year TCI merge. Its producer and required period/coverage contract remain unresolved for this assessment.

The ordered author workflow uses directory macros to locate its inputs and registered sibling do-files. A consistent working-copy root and mapping of those inputs/includes must be configured before a run.

The authors describe separate announced/enacted and as-effective spreadsheets with later updates, but the exact files, country-level source map, effective-date rules and workbook vintage are not supplied. Forward-year files are generated from the announced/enacted source.

evidence.description: README describes the supplied Stata preparation and analysis workflow.
evidence.quote:
This replication package contains the Stata code required to prepare the data and reproduce 
all tables and figures reported in the manuscript and the Online Appendix. The files are 
designed to be executed sequentially, beginning with the master do-file.

evidence.description: README identifies 0_master.do as the ordered master driver.
evidence.quote: The file 0_master.do is a master do-file that executes all remaining do-files in the correct sequence.

evidence.description: README says user-written packages are handled by SSC setup commands.
evidence.quote:
Some portions of the code rely on user-written Stata packages (e.g., reghdfe). The 
do-files include commands to automatically install required packages using ssc install 
if they are not already available on the user's system.

evidence.description: README calls the bundled CSV a BvD identifier list used to retrieve the sample.
evidence.quote:
The file primary_sample_BVD_IDs.csv contains Bureau van Dijk (BvD) firm identifiers 
for all firms included in the primary sample (417,161 unique firms). Users with access 
to Orbis may import these identifiers directly into Orbis to retrieve the corresponding 
firm-level data.

evidence.description: Datasheet names Orbis and its web interface.
evidence.quote:
a. Orbis data
              • Source: Moody’s (formerly Bureau van Dijk) Orbis database; accessed via the Orbis
                  web interface.

evidence.description: Datasheet distinguishes 504 initial text files and a second supplemental Orbis extraction.
evidence.quote:
We selected the required variables capturing financial statement and ownership
           information and downloaded the data in March 2022 as 504 individual .txt files due to
           size restrictions imposed by the Orbis web interface. The datasets included firm
           identifiers such as firm name and the Bureau van Dijk (BvD) ID number. A second
           data extraction was conducted in March 2022 to obtain depreciation expense and long-
           term debt variables that were not included in the initial download.

evidence.description: Datasheet identifies the World Bank Doing Business Paying Taxes source and machine-readable download.
evidence.quote:
b. Primary Tax Complexity Measure:
      • Source: World Bank’s Doing Business Survey; obtained from the Paying Taxes
         component of the survey (Methodology for Paying Taxes).
      • We downloaded the data in March 2022 in machine-readable format. We then merged
         these data with the Orbis data. No manual data entry was involved.

evidence.description: Datasheet describes hand-collected statutory rates and later rate-event/reduced-rate updates.
evidence.quote:
c. Statutory corporate income tax rate data:
       • Sources: Hand-collected from public sources, including tax rate tables and publications
          from the Tax Foundation, OECD, KMPG, PWC, and EY, as well as news articles,
          government announcements, and domestic law.
       • We manually collected statutory tax rate data in February and March 2022 and entered
          it into Excel. Information on tax rate change events and data on reduced corporate tax
          rates was subsequently collected in September 2022, April 2023, January 2025, and
          March 2025. These data were then merged with the Orbis data.

evidence.description: Datasheet names the WDI macro controls and a February 2023 machine-readable download.
evidence.quote:
d. Country-level macroeconomic controls:
      • Source: World Bank’s World Development Indicators; obtained from the public
         database (World Development Indicators | DataBank).
      • We downloaded the data in February 2023 in machine-readable format. We then
         merged these data with the Orbis data. No manual data entry was involved.

evidence.description: Datasheet names a September 2023 WGI download.
evidence.quote:
e. Country-level institutional controls:
      • Source: World Bank’s Worldwide Governance Indicators; obtained from the public
         database (Home | Worldwide Governance Indicators).
      • We downloaded the data in September 2023 in machine-readable format. We then
         merged these data with the Orbis data. No manual data entry was involved.

evidence.description: Datasheet identifies the EC 2020 EATR report and manual Excel extraction.
evidence.quote:
f.   EATR data:
               • Source: Effective Tax Levels using the Devereux/Griffith Methodology and as
                  reported in Spengel et al. (2020); obtained from the report published by the European
                  Commission (final_report_2020_effective_tax_levels_revised_en.pdf).
               • We manually extracted the data from the publicly available PDF report in October
                  2023 and entered it into Excel. These data were then merged with the Orbis data.

evidence.description: Datasheet identifies Compustat Global, WRDS and fiscal years 2012–2019.
evidence.quote:
g. Compustat Global data:
             • Source: Compustat Global Database; obtained via the WRDS web access.
             • We downloaded data in February 2025 for fiscal years 2012-2019 in machine-readable
                format. We then applied the relevant code to compute aggregate effective tax rates and
                merged the resulting data with the Orbis data. No manual data entry was involved.

evidence.description: Datasheet identifies Hassan tax-policy-risk input and country-year aggregation.
evidence.quote:
h. Political risk data:
               • Source: Tax policy risk data from Hassan et al. (2019); obtained from the public
                   website (www.firmlevelrisk.com).
               • We downloaded firm-level data in August 2023 in machine-readable format. We then
                   applied the relevant code to compute country-year averages and merged the resulting
                   data with the Orbis data. No manual data entry was involved.

evidence.description: Datasheet identifies the 2015 OECD survey and manual extraction.
evidence.quote:
i.   Tax enforcement data:
                • Source: 2015 OECD Tax Administration Survey; obtained from the OECD website
                    (Tax Administration 2015 | OECD).
                • We manually extracted the data from the publicly available PDF report in April 2023
                    and entered it into Excel. These data were then merged with the Orbis data.

evidence.description: Datasheet identifies the TCI download and author-code backfill.
evidence.quote:
j.   Tax Complexity index:
                • Source: Tax Complexity Index published by Hoppe et al. (2023); obtained from the
                   public website (Tax Complexity Index).
                • We downloaded the data in February 2025 in machine-readable format. We then
                   applied the relevant code to backfill missing values of the index and merged the
                   resulting data with the Orbis data. No manual data entry was involved.

evidence.description: Datasheet separately names World Bank interest payments and IMF debt and primary balance.
evidence.quote:
k. Additional country-level fiscal controls:
              • Sources: Data on government interest was obtained from the World Bank (Interest
                  payments (% of revenue) | Data); data on central government gross debt and
                  government primary balance was obtained from the IMF (IMF DataMapper).
              • We downloaded the data in July 2025 in machine-readable format. We then merged
                  these data with the Orbis data. No manual data entry was involved.

evidence.description: TCI input field contract: country, countryisocode, year and TaxComplexityIndex.
evidence.quote:
import excel "$adddatadir\tax_complexity_index.xlsx", sheet("Original Data") firstrow clear

* Drop missings observations

	drop if countryisocode==""

evidence.description: TCI code reads country_years, merges, backfills and saves its result.
evidence.quote:
use "$adddatadir\country_years.dta", clear

	merge 1:1 countryisocode year using "$adddatadir\tax_complexity_raw.dta"
	drop _merge

* Sort data by country ISO code and year

	sort countryisocode year

* Backfill missing values within country data 

	egen countries=group(countryisocode)
	xtset countries year 

	forvalues i = 1/5 {
		replace TaxComplexityIndex = TaxComplexityIndex[_n+1] ///
		if missing(TaxComplexityIndex)&countryisocode==countryisocode[_n+1]
		}
		
* Drop missing values

	drop if TaxComplexityIndex==.

* Rename variable 

	rename TaxComplexityIndex TaxComplexityIndexBackfilled

	save "$adddatadir\tax_complexity_index_backfilled.dta", replace

evidence.description: Risk source fields are converted to country-year averages.
evidence.quote:
import delimited "$adddatadir\firmquarter_2022q1.csv", clear

* Generate vayear and quarter

	gen year=substr(date,1,4)
	destring year, replace

	gen quarter=substr(date,6,1)
	destring quarter, replace

* Generate grouping variables

	egen country_year=group(hqcountrycode year)
	egen country_year_quarter=group(hqcountrycode year quarter)

* Keep only observations with available tax risk data

	drop if priskt_tax==. 

* Compute country-year averages

	bysort country_year: egen mean_taxriskyear = mean(priskt_tax)

* Keep one observation per country-year

	duplicates drop country_year, force

	keep date year mean_taxriskyear hqcountrycode

	rename hqcountrycode countryisocode 

	save "$adddatadir\firm_tax_risk.dta", replace

evidence.description: Compustat fields and country/year aggregation produce cash ETR.
evidence.quote:
import delimited "$adddatadir\compustatglobal.csv", clear

* Restrict to countries in primary sample

	keep if fic=="AUT"|fic=="BEL"|fic=="BGR"|fic=="HRV"|fic=="CZE"|fic=="EST" ///
	|fic=="FIN"|fic=="FRA"|fic=="DEU"|fic=="GRC"|fic=="HUN"|fic=="ISL"|fic=="ITA" ///
	|fic=="LVA"|fic=="LTU"|fic=="LUX"|fic=="MLT"|fic=="NLD"|fic=="NZL"|fic=="NOR" ///
	|fic=="POL"|fic=="PRT"|fic=="ROU"|fic=="SVK"|fic=="SVN"|fic=="KOR"|fic=="ESP" ///
	|fic=="SWE"


* Set spi to zero if missing

	replace spi=0 if spi==. 
	gen denominator=pi-spi

* Generate one-year cash ETR 

	gen cash_etr=txpd/denominator
	replace cash_etr=. if denominator<0
	replace cash_etr=. if txpd<0
	replace cash_etr=. if cash_etr>=1

* Drop observations with missing cash ETRs

	drop if cash_etr==.

* Generate country-year groupings

	egen country_year=group(fic fyear)

* Sum total assets by country_year group

	bysort country_year: egen assets_cy_cashetr=sum(at) 

* Generate asset weights

	gen w_cash_etr=cash_etr*at/assets_cy_cashetr

* Sum individual weights

	bysort country_year: egen cash_etr_aggr=sum(w_cash_etr)

	duplicates drop fic fyear, force

* Keep key variables and multiple ETRs by 100

	keep fic fyear cash_etr_aggr  

	replace cash_etr_aggr=cash_etr_aggr*100

* Rename variables

	rename fyear year
	rename fic countrycode

	save "$adddatadir\shevlin_et_al_aggregatedETRs.dta", replace

actions.description: Obtain the author-described main Orbis extract using the supplied sample identifiers and documented filters.
steps: Use the bundled BvD ID list only as a retrieval list. Obtain the 504 numbered main files through an authorized Orbis route using the author’s active-company/geography/ownership criteria and 2012–2019 financial fields.
Stage the files in the configured working-copy input tree without changing sample or analysis rules.
validation: Check the numbered set, BvD IDs, status/NACE filters, year columns and required financial field families before sample preparation.

actions.description: Obtain and stage the separate 37-file supplemental Orbis pull before the BvD-key merge.
steps: Retrieve the supplemental depreciation/long-term-debt files for the sample IDs through an authorized route.
Preserve the supplied producer; confirm raw field labels and keep the supplemental merge on bvdidnumber.
validation: Check all 37 files, BvD match and depreciation/long-term-debt years before the main sample merge.

actions.description: Request the exact country-year master or its supported producer specification.
steps: Ask the authors for country_years.dta source/producer, country list, year endpoints and staging order.
Preserve the 1:1 countryisocode/year TCI merge and following author backfill.
validation: Confirm key types, unique country-year rows and required country/year coverage.

actions.description: Recover the exact Paying Taxes workbook or its source-series mapping.
steps: Request the March 2022 machine-readable input or exact historical series mapping; do not infer fields from a different release.
Stage the workbook’s Data sheet with ISO2, year and the listed variables.
validation: Check all fields, keys and country-year data before the country merge.

actions.description: Obtain the four WDI indicator codes and exact macro-control input contract.
steps: Request the author’s WDI codes, units and transformations for GDP growth, inflation, unemployment and GDP per capita.
Prepare countryisocode/year rows in country_controls.xlsx only after definitions are confirmed.
validation: Confirm each field and required 2012–2019 sample-country coverage.

actions.description: Recover the author’s WGI 2023 workbook or exact variable crosswalk.
steps: Request the September 2023 vintage or source-variable mapping for gee and pve, plus ISO2/year handling.
Do not substitute the recalculated current release without author-supported mapping.
validation: Confirm iso2, year, gee and pve and required sample coverage.

actions.description: Recover the exact TCI download and its field/vintage contract.
steps: Request the February 2025 source file or exact public wave/vintage with country, countryisocode, year and TaxComplexityIndex.
Supply country_years separately and retain the author merge/backfill.
validation: Check country-year uniqueness and years before backfill.

actions.description: Recover the author’s exact tax-policy-risk CSV vintage.
steps: Request the August 2023 author file or exact documented public download matching firmquarter_2022q1.csv.
Confirm date/hqcountrycode/priskt_tax and preserve the country-year averaging code.
validation: Check source history, country code conversion and required 2012–2019 observations.

actions.description: Recover the author’s cited EATR report table or original workbook.
steps: Request the exact cited European Commission 2020 table or eatr.xlsx, including EATR definition, country codes and report years.
Stage the wide country/year columns consumed by the supplied reshape.
validation: Confirm country-year coverage and the reshaped countryisocode/year/EATR fields.

actions.description: Stage the local Compustat Global candidate as the author-required CSV after confirming year and country coverage.
steps: Confirm the local COMP.G_FUNDA candidate covers 2012–2019 and the author FIC country set; the one-row probe only confirms field names.
Export fic, fyear, spi, pi, txpd and at to compustatglobal.csv.
Retain the author’s missing-spi rule and asset-weighted country-year ETR computation.
validation: Check fields, fiscal years, FIC codes and countrycode/year/cash_etr_aggr output before merging.

actions.description: Recover the author’s OECD 2015 extraction workbook and exact report tables/years.
steps: Request tax_enforcement_OECD.xls or exact table/page and extraction instructions, including country/year, verification_all, revenue denominator and units.
Do not substitute a later OECD survey or independently rebuild missing values.
validation: Check country/year keys, selected survey year and the numerator/denominator used in analysis.

actions.description: Confirm the exact IMF debt series, sector, unit and vintage.
steps: Request the IMF DataMapper series code and central-government definition/vintage used in government_debt_IMF.xlsx.
After identification, prepare countryisocode and annual government_debtIMF year columns for the supplied reshape.
validation: Verify sector, units, country/year mapping and required period.

actions.description: Acquire the author-specified World Bank interest series and prepare its expected workbook.
steps: Use the named Interest payments (% of revenue) indicator as a candidate and preserve the author’s July 2025 vintage if available.
Confirm required sample-country years and map to the existing wide workbook contract.
validation: Check 2012–2019 coverage, percent-of-revenue units and countryisocode3digit/year output.

actions.description: Confirm the exact IMF primary-balance series, sector, units and vintage.
steps: Request the author’s IMF DataMapper series code and definition for government primary balance, including sector, units and fiscal/calendar year.
Prepare countryisocode and annual primary_balanceIMF columns only after source identification.
validation: Check required country/year coverage and primary-balance definition before merge.

actions.description: Request both author tax-rate spreadsheets and source crosswalk; preserve them as separate inputs.
steps: Request announced/enacted and as-effective workbooks with per-country sources, event dates, rate definitions and update history through March 2025.
Stage countryisocode/year/anneffective_TR and countryisocode/year/effective_TR separately; let 0_3 create t+1/t+2 files.
validation: Check unique country-year keys, rate definitions and forward-year coverage.

actions.description: Map registered scripts into one working-copy root while preserving author sequence.
steps: Bind the existing directory globals consistently across registered preparation and analysis scripts.
Map master includes to registered sibling files; masked tokens prevent exact replacement proposals.
Preserve 0_1–0_4, then 1, 2 and the supplied stacked branch.
validation: Review all input/output mappings as a coherent set and confirm registered includes resolve before an authorized run.

actions.description: Prepare required Stata commands reported unavailable.
steps: Before a separate authorized run, confirm winsor2 and outreg2 in the intended Stata environment and use the author-documented SSC setup if still unavailable.
Assess Stata 18 compatibility with the documented Stata 19 without changing estimators.
validation: Record exact package/runtime versions and command availability; do not modify the authored analysis.

review_notes: The registered entry point is 0_master.do. README supports ordered preparation, the primary analysis and the separate secondary stacked DiD branch; both remain in full_pipeline.
primary_sample_BVD_IDs.csv is an identifier-only retrieval aid, not the Orbis financial dataset or an author-prepared analysis panel; no analysis_only scope is supported.
The main Orbis and supplemental Orbis pulls are separate jointly required inputs. The supplemental producer is supplied and is joined on BvD identifiers; no raw-file alternatives were invented.

Targeted frozen-catalog queries identify one local Compustat Global candidate. A one-row probe confirms its six fields but not fiscal-year or country coverage. Catalog misses for other named products are not access-barrier evidence.
No author program, statistical model, SAS startup, installation or data download was run.

Process limitation: the approved source viewer left some master/country setup ranges unread. This is recorded as coverage context only; it is not evidence that code, an input producer, or data are absent.
